The issue is occurring in the test `testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode()` of `TarArchiveOutputStreamTest`. The test is trying to add a directory to a TAR Archive with a name longer than 100 bytes, which generates an exception due to the size in the header exceeding the allowed limit.

Looking at the method `TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(ArchiveEntry)`, we can see that there is a check for the length of the entry name. If the name is too long, different handling mechanisms are applied based on the `longFileMode` set.

In the code snippet provided, there are conditions for handling long file names based on the `longFileMode`. If the `longFileMode` is `LONGFILE_POSIX`, a PAX header with the path is added. However, in the case of a long file name in POSIX mode and when the filename is a directory, the `path` PAX header is added without considering the length constraint. This may lead to exceeding the header size limit in the TAR Archive, causing the exception mentioned in the bug report.

To fix this issue, we need to ensure that the length of the directory name is taken into account when adding PAX headers in the `TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry()` method.

Next, I will suggest the best methods to be fixed based on this diagnosis.
```
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ArchiveEntry)
```
